planting.note: Direct sow or start transplants 3-4 weeks before setting out after soil has warmed; in zone 9 sow March-July for successive summer harvests. Unlike its relative winter melon, fuzzy gourd is picked young and immature rather than left to mature and cure.

directions: Sow seeds an inch deep in well-drained, fertile, moderately moist soil in full sun, and grow on a sturdy trellis to keep the fuzzy fruit clean and straight. Fuzzy gourd is a smaller, fast-maturing variety group of the same species as winter melon, but it is harvested young while the cylindrical fruit is still tender, pale green, and covered in the soft fuzz that gives it its name, rather than being left to mature into the large, waxy-coated winter melon. It is a staple vegetable in Cantonese and Southeast Asian cooking, prized for its mild flavor and tender texture in soups, stir-fries, and braises, where it readily absorbs the flavors of broth, meat, and aromatics. Harvest fruits at 6-10 inches long while the skin fuzz is still soft, since older fruit develops a tougher, less palatable rind; frequent picking encourages continued production through the hot summer months that this heat-loving vine relishes.
